study_identification_part.si_4_title: Regional, circuit and network heterogeneity of brain abnormalities in psychiatric disorders

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: Hierarchical Bayesian Regression (HBR) was used to build the normative model. The HBR modeled site and sex effects with random slopes, intercepts and noise. Shared prior distributions were imposed over site-specific and sex-specific model parameters using a partial-pooling approach. PCNtoolkit v0.16 was used for implementation.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: To account for these site-related effects, we built our normative model using HBR, which successfully accommodates signal and noise variance in multisite data by estimating different but connected mean and variance components through shared prior distributions across sites; Following stratification of our sample into training and test subsets, for each of the 1,032 parcellated brain regions, we fitted separate HBRs. The HBRs modelled site and sex effects with random slopes, intercepts and noise, to model GMV as a function of age, sex and site in the training data

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: Gray matter volume (GMV) was the response variable modeled. GMV was estimated using the CAT12 VBM pipeline. Regional GMV estimates were parcellated into 1,032 brain regions (1,000 cortical from Schaefer parcellation and 32 subcortical from Tian parcellation). Before modeling, regional GMV estimates were subjected to a Box-Cox transformation to ensure normality.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: GMV was estimated using the CAT12 VBM pipeline; Normative models estimate the mean and variance (referred to as a normative range) of a response variable (for example, GMV) from a set of clinically relevant covariates; to model GMV as a function of age, sex and site in the training data
nm2_2_response_variable.location: Segal2023.pdf.md: Methods / Normative modeling; Methods / MRI preprocessing

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: Age, sex, and site were used as covariates in the normative model. The HBR modeled site and sex effects with random slopes, intercepts and noise. Site was included to account for scanner- and site-related variability that confounds multisite analyses.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: model GMV as a function of age, sex and site in the training data; For the model to accurately parse variance attributable to age, sex and site, sufficient observations are required for any given combination of these variables
